item.title: Time Is the One Thing AI Doesn’t Compress
item.dc:creator: Stéphane Cuenat
item.description:
In this newsletter I have mostly written about how AI changes processes, and how a company should reinvent itself around it. One aspect I never touched: time.

The feeling of having no time

When we use AI (and I include myself first), we want to do more, always faster, as if we had no time anymore. That feeling is only a feeling, and it may make us lose more than we gain.

Learning takes time. That time is almost incompressible, because learning means understanding.

To solve a problem, spend most of your time understanding it.

The first signs

Someone answered one of my questions with “I don’t know, Claude Code did it.” For me, that is one of the first signs that we didn’t take the time to really get into the problem.

item.title: Fewer Coefficients: Why We Need Less Data, Not More
item.dc:creator: Stéphane Cuenat
item.description:
We keep producing more data, only for it to end up in dashboards. That’s not what we need.

Fit a polynomial of degree through points and it hits every one of them, yet swings wildly in between (Runge’s phenomenon). A low-order fit

captures the shape and predicts where we haven’t measured.

A useful test: does this output change a decision? If a dashboard tile never alters what anyone does, it’s a coefficient that isn’t pulling its weight.
